nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: For a few seconds, I don’t remember what I was supposed to do today.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Then my phone vibrates, and the day remembers me first.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The room is familiar enough that I could find everything without turning on the light.

choices.text: Look at the clothes on the chair

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The glass reflects more of the room than the view outside. The street is carrying on without me.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Black screen. A faint reflection of the bed. Whatever I was doing last night can wait.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: A chair has become a wardrobe by administrative default.

nodes.speaker: Phone
nodes.text: Nearside — Someone liked you.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: A notification. The kind that promises absolutely nothing and still manages to ask for a little hope.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: There was a time when a match felt like something had happened. Now it’s mostly a tiny administrative task that might eventually become disappointment.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Say hello. Ask a question. Try not to sound like you’re asking for an interview. Wait. Pretend you didn’t check.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The room settles back into its small noises. A little later, the screen lights again.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: I turn the phone face down. The street carries on without needing an answer from me.

nodes.speaker: Phone
nodes.text: Nearside — New message.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Another one. All right. That is technically different.

choices.text: Leave the phone alone for today

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text:
The message can wait. I put the phone away. Nothing has to happen today.

END OF DEMO — THE FIRST MATCH

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text:
Maria’s photo is dark and slightly off-centre; hair partly hides her face. Her profile reads: “I like quiet cafés, bad horror films, and people who can sit in silence without trying to fix it.”

My own profile mentions bad horror films and says: “I have strong opinions about very unimportant things.”

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Strong brand. Very relatable. Mine is “look away from the camera and hope that counts as a personality.”

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Then I think you’ve achieved it. Congratulations, genuinely.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Honestly? You sounded like a person. That’s rarer on here than it should be.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Only for a very boring case. The suspect is bad lighting.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Okay, important question. Is your profile photo intentionally mysterious, or did you just not want to take another one?

choices.text: It’s called building a brand. The brand is “doesn’t know where to put their hands in photos.”
I was going for “person who has never been photographed under normal circumstances.”
I just don’t take many photos. What made you message me?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: That’s comforting. I was worried everyone on here had a five-year plan.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I think the bar is lower than that. You can start with “I like it” and we’ll see where the wheels come off.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: No. Sometimes I make them do a written test. This is the relaxed version.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Your profile says you like bad horror films. Is that something you actually watch, or something you put there to look employable?

choices.text: A bit of both. I contain multitudes, most of them poorly organised.
I do like them. I just don’t know if I’m interesting enough to make it a conversation.
Do you always interview people this quickly?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I was going to delete this app again tonight, actually.

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: Why didn’t you?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I had a very convincing speech prepared. Then I got distracted and forgot to delete it.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Also, your profile made me laugh. Not in a “laughing at you” way. I should probably have led with that.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The typing indicator disappears, then comes back.

choices.text: What are you actually hoping to find on here?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: It does, doesn’t it? Which is probably why the app keeps making it feel like a job.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I’m allowed one contradictory opinion per day. I used today’s early.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: That’s a fair answer. Better than pretending you’ve got it all worked out.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I’d like to meet someone I actually want to see again. I don’t think I can know much more than that before meeting them.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Something that feels easy to talk to. Not effortless. Just… not like I’m trying to sell myself to a stranger.

choices.text: That sounds optimistic for someone about to delete the app.
I don’t know what I’m looking for yet.
Are you looking for something serious?

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: For once, the conversation hasn’t become an interview.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: This might be a slightly strange question.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: There’s a café I like. It’s a little tucked away, kind of downstairs from the street. I’m free this afternoon. Would you want to meet there?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: How about four? Gives us time to become different people before then.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I was going for “quiet place with good tea.” Mystery is included at no extra charge.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: It’s called The Lantern Room. Usually quiet around four. I can send you the address so you can check it out.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: That’s completely fair. The Lantern Room is public, but if you’d rather pick somewhere more central, I’m happy to.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Of course. We don’t have to turn a conversation into a calendar invitation.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: No worries. I’m glad I asked. And I hope your day gets a bit better, even if it doesn’t involve a suspicious downstairs café.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: No pressure, by the way. I know meeting a stranger because an app said so is a weird thing to do. We could just keep talking. Or not. I won’t be offended if today isn’t your day.

choices.text: Yeah. I’d like that. What time?
A downstairs café? Are you trying to make this sound like the beginning of a mystery?
What’s the place called? And is it busy?
I’d rather meet somewhere public and easy to find for a first date.
I’m not sure about today. Can we talk a little more first?
I don’t think I’m up for meeting today, but thanks for asking.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Four o’clock, a public café, an address I can look up. I still get to decide.

choices.text: The Lantern Room works. Let’s meet at four.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I’ll send the pin. If the map decides to lead you into a wall, it’s not my fault.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I’m very good at reassurance. Less good at directions.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text:
The conversation stays open. There is no appointment to keep, and no debt attached to being asked.

END OF DEMO — THE FIRST MATCH

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text:
I set the phone down. It was an invitation, and I gave an answer. That is allowed.

END OF DEMO — THE FIRST MATCH

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: It’s not the outfit that takes time. It’s deciding whether this is worth the effort.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: If this is awkward, at least I’ll be awkward in something I can breathe in.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: No harm in looking like I meant to leave the house.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: It’s a coffee, not a diplomatic summit.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: I look like myself. That should be enough. I spend another minute checking anyway.

choices.text: Put the phone away and leave

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The Lantern Room. Four o’clock. A public place, a little below street level. The address is saved.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: “Less good at directions.” I catch myself smiling at a message that isn’t even particularly funny.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Muted traffic, shopfront reflections, the entrance a little below street level.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: I could still turn around. The thought is comforting, mostly because I don’t actually want to.

choices.text: Message Maria that I can’t make it, and head home

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text:
I let her know instead of leaving her waiting. “Thanks for telling me. Get home safe,” she replies.

END OF DEMO — THE FIRST MATCH

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Maria is already there. Dark layers, hair partly falling across her face. She tries to look composed, then seems to wonder if she succeeded.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I knew it. The map is jealous.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I did worry the entrance looked like it belonged to a storage room. It has that energy.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: It is. If it turns out to be a very elaborate trap, I’ll be just as embarrassed as you.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Hi. You made it.

choices.text: Hi. Sorry, I wasn’t sure if I was in the right place.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Do you want to sit by the window, or would you rather have a little more space?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I had a whole opening line planned.

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: What happened to it?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: You arrived and I forgot it. So, already a successful evening for my brain.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: It was incredible. Historians would have argued about it for centuries.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: No, no. It would lose the natural spontaneity that made it terrible.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Good. We can both be disappointing at the same time.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: What do I say?

choices.text: You can still use it. I’ll pretend to arrive again.
That’s all right. I didn’t prepare one either.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Have you looked at the menu, or are you also going to make a life-changing decision based on the pictures?

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: I usually choose the thing I can pronounce.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: That’s a sound system. Mine is choosing something, then wondering if the other thing would’ve been better.

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: So you regret every drink?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Not every drink. Only the ones I ordered while someone was watching.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Good choice. I was going to get tea too, but now I have to pretend I wasn’t copying you.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Fair. I respect a beverage with a job.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Excellent. I’ll try not to judge you. I make no promises about the cake.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: We can take a minute. The menu isn’t going anywhere. Probably.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: What do I say?

choices.text: Coffee. I need all the help I can get.
Something sweet. I have no dignity to defend.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Can I ask something without making this sound like a job interview?

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: You’ve already asked at least three questions. Go on.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: How long have you been on that app?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: The slow fade. They could at least send a little certificate.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I know that feeling. You get tired of it, then one conversation is decent and you start making excuses for the app.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I was trying to find out whether we both hate it equally. I can stop asking if you’d rather not talk about it.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: That’s fair. We can talk about literally anything else. The weather has done nothing wrong.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: What do I say?

choices.text: Long enough to recognise the exact moment someone stops replying.
On and off. I keep thinking it might be different if I try again.
I’d rather not compare bad dates on the first one.

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: You said my profile made you laugh. What part?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: The line about “strong opinions about very unimportant things”. It sounded like something you’d say out loud, not something a committee approved.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Please do. I was trying to give a compliment without making it weird.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: No. I got that it made me smile. The rest is me guessing. I’m not secretly a detective.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: What do I say?

choices.text: That’s oddly specific. I’ll take it.
You got all that from one profile?

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: What do you do when you’re not on the app?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Very glamorous things. I make tea and forget it’s there. I watch films I complain about. Sometimes I walk until I realise I don’t know where I am, which sounds more poetic than it is.

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: What kind of films?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Horror, mostly. The bad ones are easier to love. You can tell the director cared, even when the monster looks like a damp curtain.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: When I know I’m allowed to stop being scared afterwards.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I’m full of sensible answers. I save them for first dates so people don’t discover my true nature.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: What do I say?

choices.text: That’s a suspiciously sensible answer for a horror fan.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I almost cancelled, by the way.

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: Why?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I got dressed, then sat on my bed for twenty minutes trying to convince myself I was tired. I wasn’t even that tired.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: That makes me feel a little less ridiculous. Not that I was asking you to fix it.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Who won?

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: Apparently the person who wanted tea.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: A terrifying negotiator.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: You don’t have to. I only said it because it was true, not because you owe me the same.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: What do I say?

choices.text: I had to negotiate with myself too. It was a difficult meeting.
I don’t usually tell people that kind of thing this early.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: If you get the tea, the one with the orange peel is good. The other one tastes like someone described a garden from memory.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I have strong opinions about very unimportant things.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: A few times. It’s quiet. I like places where you don’t have to compete with the music to hear someone.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: That was the plan, yes. It would’ve been awkward if I had to lip-read the entire date.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: What do I say?

choices.text: You sound like you’ve reviewed the entire menu.
So you brought me here because you can hear me?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: How have your days been lately?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I know that loop. Sometimes you only notice how small it’s got when you try to explain it to someone.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: That can be its own kind of tiring. You don’t have to give me the full report.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Then this is a point in favour of doing things. Even if the thing is drinking tea with a stranger.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Okay. What would you rather talk about?

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: What do I say?

choices.text: Mostly the same. Work, home, phone, sleep. Repeat.
A bit full-on, actually. I haven’t had much time to think.
Pretty good. I’m trying to do more things instead of sitting around.
I’d rather not get into work tonight.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Are you always this hard to read, or am I just doing an impressive job of making this awkward?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Fair. I asked that badly. You don’t have to perform being comfortable for me.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Devastating. I’ll have to update my résumé.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: You’re right. Sorry. I meant it as a joke, but it didn’t land that way.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: What do I say?

choices.text: I’m still deciding how comfortable I am.
Maybe you’re just not as charming as you think.
That’s a pretty personal thing to ask someone you’ve just met.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: That cake has been cut into a shape no cake should have to experience.

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: Maybe it’s modern art.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Then I don’t understand the art. I’d still eat it.

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: You use humour to avoid silence?

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Sometimes. Silence is fine. I just panic when I think someone thinks the silence is my fault.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Good. Then I’ll try not to fill every gap with cake criticism.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: What do I say?

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The cups are almost empty. The room has become familiar while we were talking.

choices.text: I’m still undecided. Let that be enough.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: She wasn’t what I expected from the photo. Or maybe the photo was just a bad way to meet a person. It wasn’t a perfect date. That might be why it felt real.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Nothing had happened that I could point to. I just hadn’t decided what I thought of her yet. That was allowed.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: I had spent the walk here preparing for an awkward hour. I hadn’t prepared for wanting it to last a little longer.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I should probably let you go before I start reviewing the furniture.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Me too. I was worried I would be very strange in person.

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: You were strange in person.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Right. Excellent. My brand is consistent.

nodes.speaker: You
nodes.text: I mean it in a good way.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I know. I think.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: I’d like that. Maybe somewhere with less complicated stairs next time.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Slow is fine. We only just met. I don’t want to skip the part where we find out if we actually get along.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: That’s okay. You don’t have to decide on the walk home.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Thanks for telling me honestly. I hope you get home safe.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: At the door, there is still a little time to say what I mean.

choices.text: I’d like to see you again.
I’d be open to meeting again. I’d rather take things slowly.
I’m glad we met. I’m not sure yet what I want.
I don’t think it’s a match for me, but I appreciate meeting you.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Outside, the street is ordinary. We each have a way home.

choices.text: Walk a little, then check the phone
Walk a little, then check the phone
Walk a little, then check the phone
Leave the phone in my pocket for tonight

nodes.speaker: Maria · message
nodes.text: I had a nice time. Also, I have just realised I spent ten minutes complaining about cake. Sorry about that.

choices.text: It was a very compelling cake review.
I had a nice time too.
Leave the message unanswered for now.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text:
END OF DEMO — THE FIRST MATCH

The evening stays what it was. What it means can wait.

She wanted to shape the evening.
